title: In 1919, a Wave of Molasses Killed 21 People in Boston

scenes.text: In 1919, a wave of molasses killed 21 people in Boston.
A 50 foot steel tank burst on a warm January day. Two point three million gallons.
scenes.keywords: huge steel storage tank old industrial

scenes.text: The wave was 25 feet high and moved at 35 miles an hour. You can't outrun that.
scenes.keywords: old Boston street 1920s black and white

scenes.text: It ripped a firehouse off its foundation and knocked a streetcar off its tracks.
Cooling molasses sets like glue. Rescuers spent four days pulling people out.
For decades, locals swore the street still smelled of molasses on hot days.

description:
On January 15, 1919, a 50-foot steel tank in Boston's North End burst and released 2.3 million gallons of molasses.
The wave was about 25 feet high and moved at roughly 35 miles an hour. It killed 21 people, injured about 150, tore a firehouse from its foundation and knocked a streetcar off its tracks. Rescuers searched for four days, and residents said the area smelled of molasses on hot days for decades.
What's the strangest disaster you've ever heard of? Comment below.
first_comment: The company that owned the tank fought the case for years, then paid about 628,000 dollars in damages. Could a 25-foot wave of syrup really be outrun? What would you have done?
